source_reviews.independent_solution: Parallel distinct planes have parallel normals. A slant line to alpha intersects it, so its direction v has nonzero normal component, and v is not parallel to the normal. The same two properties hold for beta. Equivalently the line intersects beta and cannot be perpendicular to beta, because theorem 19 with alpha and beta exchanged would then make it perpendicular to alpha. Therefore it is also a slant line to beta.

1) The planes must intersect: coincidence would make both perpendicular to the line, while parallelism would make both perpendicular by theorem 19. These exhaust alternatives to intersection for distinct planes. 2) No. If a were perpendicular to both intersecting planes, both normals would be parallel to a, forcing alpha and beta to be parallel (or coincident), contrary to alpha cap beta=m.

AB and CD both follow the common normal of alpha and beta. Their endpoints span the same perpendicular plane separation, so their lengths equal that separation. In an elementary proof, for distinct feet A,C, the coplanar normal lines and their joining lines form rectangle ABDC: AC and BD are parallel intersections of the auxiliary plane with alpha and beta; AB is parallel CD and perpendicular AC. Its opposite sides AB and CD are equal. If A=C, B=D and equality is immediate.

The segment incidence forces M-B-A and M-C-D, rather than placing M between the planes. Hence MA=MB+BA=17 cm. The normal MA is perpendicular to beta, so triangle MBC is right at B; BC=sqrt(MC^2-MB^2)=sqrt(169-144)=5 cm. The auxiliary plane MAD cuts parallel alpha and beta in parallel lines AD and BC. Triangles MBC and MAD are similar with MA/MB=17/12, giving AD=BC*17/12=85/12 cm. Both requested quantities and their independent units must be retained.

Let E be the midpoint of CD. AC=AD and BC=BD imply A and B both lie in the perpendicular-bisector plane Pi of CD, so Pi contains the noncollinear points A,B,E and is perpendicular to CD. Reflection in Pi fixes A,B and exchanges C,D. Let P,Q be midpoints of AC,BC, and let R lie on CD with CR=CD/4. Homothety with center C and ratio 1/2 sends A,B,E to P,Q,R; hence PQR is in the plane perpendicular to CD through the prescribed midpoint Q of BC. This plane cuts exactly edges CA,CB,CD and the section is triangle PQR. Let U,V be midpoints of AD,BD and let S on DC satisfy DS=CD/4. The corresponding upper plane through U cuts exactly DA,DB,DC and gives triangle UVS. Reflection in Pi maps P to U, Q to V, R to S, proving congruence. Alternatively PQ=UV=AB/2, PR=US=AE/2, QR=VS=BE/2 proves SSS. The two sections are parallel, lie on opposite sides of Pi, and do not pass through E.
